task.title: Relics: show history and diffs
task.description:
A relic is a new kind of record in Workbook, separate from tasks. It holds specs, plans, decisions, transcripts and similar material, with the same history and sharing that tasks have. A relic has a title, a type, an author, links, and content made of named parts.

Every change to a relic is already kept. This story makes that history readable and comparable, so people can review changes the way they review a pull request, and so a project can build its own viewer on the JSON.

## What this delivers

```
workbook relic show <relic>[#part] --history
workbook relic diff <relic>[#part] [<version> [<version>]]
```

- `--history` lists the recorded changes to a relic, or to one part, with author and time.
- `relic diff` is its own command. With two versions it compares them. With one it compares that version with the current one. With none it shows the latest change.
- For a part, the diff is a line-by-line comparison of the body and a field-by-field comparison of the fields. For a whole relic, it also lists parts added, removed and moved, properties changed, and links added and removed.
- A per-part list of body versions, each named by the ID of the change that saved it.
- `--json` output that carries enough for a viewer to draw a side-by-side or inline diff without calling Git.

## Rules that matter

- Diffs are computed when asked. Nothing extra is stored.
- A version name is the change ID, never a Git commit ID, so a name noted earlier still works after history is replayed.
- A body whose format is not text is reported as changed, with sizes, and is not compared line by line.
- History served from the index must agree with history read from Git.
- A stale edit that did not change the text (its starting version was out of date) is shown in history under its author and marked as not applied.

## Done when

- Any two versions of any part can be compared from the command line and from JSON.
- History for a relic edited from two clones shows every change once, in a stable order.
- The relic benchmark gains history and diff timings for a 100 KiB body edited 100 times.
- The reference documents both commands.

## Not in this story

The web page that draws these diffs, and merge records, which arrive with automatic merging.

## Where the design is

The approved design is "Workbook Relics Design" (2026-11-21). It is kept out of the repository. Until "Relics: teach agents to use relics and store the design as the first relic" is done, an untracked copy sits at `specs/2026-11-21-relics-design.html` in Dylan's checkout. After that, read the relic. This description carries what the story needs, and the design wins where the two disagree.
